66	   - **An input the task file calls required and the issue does not carry stops the
67	     run.** Say which one was missing and park this item (`needs-human` +
68	     `task:needs-human-action` — the item has to be re-created carrying it). Never
69	     reconstruct it — searching for the issue by title, taking the newest branch, or
70	     inferring the scope substitutes another run's inputs for this one's, and the run
71	     then reports success on work nobody asked for.
72	   - If the work turns out empty, that is a legitimate result. "The work ran and
73	     produced nothing" is an outcome; deciding not to run is not yours to make.
74	
75	5. **Verify your outcome in code** against the task's declared ceiling before you
76	   finish. A `none` task may not open a PR; an `open-pr` task may not merge one.
77	   Exceeding the ceiling is a failure, not a success with a surprise.
78	
79	6. **Converge the issue exactly once — in code, not by hand.** One command
80	   performs every side effect the transition needs: the comment, the label swap,
81	   the outcome label, the `claudinite-task-exec` record on the item, the close
82	   with the right state reason, the request write-back, and the release of
83	   anything that was blocked on this item.
84	
85	   ```bash
86	   node <engine>/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue <n> \
87	     --outcome done|approval|action|decision|failure \
88	     --summary '<what happened>' [--pr <n>]
89	   ```
90	
91	   **You supply the judgment — which outcome, and the prose.** Everything below
92	   is how to choose; nothing below is yours to perform. If the command refuses,
93	   read what it says: it means this item is not yours to converge, and doing it
94	   by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`.
95	
96	   | label | when |
97	   |---|---|
98	   | `task:done` | succeeded, nothing pending — close the issue |
99	   | `needs-human` | anything else — leave the issue open, and add exactly one of the four below |
100	
101	   Every park wears `needs-human` **and** one sub-label saying what you are asking
102	   a person for. Pick by the REMEDY, not by how the run felt:
103	
104	   | sub-label | when |
105	   |---|---|
106	   | `task:needs-human-approval` | you succeeded and deliberately left an unmerged PR. Name it; the human merges or closes it |
107	   | `task:needs-human-action` | something outside the code must change before this can run: a secret, a scope, a routine's wiring, an input this item never carried |
108	   | `task:needs-human-decision` | you stopped mid-flight and what happens next is a choice — you ran out of time, or you exceeded the declared ceiling and someone must say whether that stands |

## Summary of findings across three transcripts

### Log 1 — issue-157 (2026-08-13T2146Z, basics/update apply-stage)

**Candidate 1 — Signal type 3 (long wall-time wait), MEASURED**
Evidence: entries ~190–226. A `Monitor` task (`byoihpmee`) was started at **21:22:29Z** with a 20-minute timeout (`1200000ms`), running a `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" .../check-runs` polling loop against PR #156's conformance check on commit `b85d4b1`. The check itself started at 21:22:26Z and completed at 21:22:32Z — **6 seconds later**. But the Monitor never reported completion; it timed out at **21:42:29.997Z**, a full 20 minutes wasted. When the agent then queried status directly via `mcp__github__pull_request_read` (`get_check_runs`), the answer ("success") came back instantly. Root cause surfaces a few lines later: a raw `curl` using the shell's `$GITHUB_TOKEN` against the GitHub REST API returned `"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App"` — the token was never usable for direct API calls in this session type, so the curl-based poll was doomed from the start and silently looped for the full timeout doing nothing useful.
**Proposed durable fix**: when an executor session needs to wait on a GitHub check-run/CI status, build the `Monitor` poll loop around the **MCP GitHub tool** (`pull_request_read` / `get_check_runs`) rather than raw `curl` + shell `$GITHUB_TOKEN` — that token is not wired for direct GitHub API access in this environment, so a curl-based poll can fail silently and burn its entire timeout. Record this as a scheduler/executor-pack convention (it's a pattern the executor routine itself uses repeatedly).
**Confidence**: high — measurable, recurs anywhere the executor waits on CI, and the fix is a concrete tooling swap, not a permission workaround.

**Candidate 2 — Signal type 2 (suboptimal agent action, recurring across sessions)**
Evidence: issue-157 entries ~255–269 and issue-159 entries ~287–319 (same script, same failure, two different sessions). `verify-outcome.mjs` exports a function but has no CLI entrypoint; the executor's only way to invoke it is an inline `node -e "import(...)...”` one-liner, which reliably trips the Claude Code auto-mode classifier ("Permission for this action was denied by the classifier"). In issue-159 this cost ~4 minutes (03:11:39–03:15:30) of writing/renaming three separate probe scripts (`verify-check.mjs`, `hello-tmp.mjs`, `probe1.mjs`) before one happened to pass. In issue-157 the agent instead gave up retrying and reasoned about the outcome by reading the source directly.
**Proposed durable fix**: give `verify-outcome.mjs` (and any other scheduler helper meant to be invoked ad hoc by the executor) a plain CLI entrypoint (`node verify-outcome.mjs --outcome merged-pr --opened=false --merged=true`) instead of requiring an inline `node -e "import(...)"` snippet — a plain script invocation is both more classifier-friendly and removes the need to reconstruct the call shape each run.
**Confidence**: medium — the underlying trigger (classifier denial) borders the excluded "routing around a denial" category, but the fix here is a genuine tooling/ergonomics improvement to the project's own script, not a bypass technique, and it recurred verbatim in 2 of 3 sessions.

### Log 2 — issue-159 (2026-08-14T0317Z, basics/update apply-stage)
Same two candidates above appear here (Monitor pattern was avoided this time via `run_in_background: sleep 60` instead of curl+Monitor, so no new wait-time waste; the `verify-outcome.mjs` classifier friction repeats and is quantified above). No further new durable signal beyond what's already captured.

### Log 3 — issue-161 (2026-08-14T0516Z, tidy-repo/tidy-issues)
This session ran cleanly and fast (~4 minutes total). One friction point occurred: two `mcp__github__search_issues` calls with `in:title` and no `fields` filter both exceeded the MCP token limit ("result exceeds maximum allowed tokens"), forcing a fallback through saved-to-disk JSON parsed with `python3`. **This is already a documented rule** in this repo's own `claudinite-website/RULES.md` ("`mcp__github__search_issues`/`list_issues` located by title... blow the MCP token limit... Pass `fields: [...]` on the *first* call") — and that rule explicitly cites issue #161 as one of three sessions that hit this. No new lesson here; it's an existing rule that this session (chronologically) contributed to, and the third search call in this same session correctly applied `fields` afterward. Nothing else in this log rises to the durability bar — triage was fast, correct, and used the `single-issue-triage` skill as intended.

## No-comment vs candidate logs
- **candidate**: issue-157 (Monitor/curl wait-time waste; verify-outcome classifier friction)
- **candidate**: issue-159 (verify-outcome classifier friction recurrence, quantified)
- **no-comment**: issue-161 (clean run; its one friction point is already captured in existing repo rules)

## Summary

### Candidate 1 — Signal type 3 (measured wall-time waste) + Signal type 2

**Evidence**: All three sessions independently hit the exact same dead end at the queue task's final "converge item in code" step — `converge-item.mjs` fails first with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`, then (after setting it) with `#262/#260/#244 could not be read`, which each session then root-caused via env-var inspection, `gh.mjs`/`github.mjs` reading, and a manual `curl` to `api.github.com` that returns `403 GitHub access is not enabled for this session` — because this session's GitHub access is MCP-tool-only; the script needs a direct REST token the session doesn't have.

Measured from each transcript's own timestamps:
- **#244**: 13:02:25 → 13:05:30 = **3m05s**
- **#260**: 12:59:59 → 13:05:29 = **5m30s** (this one filed the dedicated gap issue, #277)
- **#262**: 13:04:55 → 13:06:58 = **2m04s** — notably, this session ran its converge step *after* #277 already existed (filed at 13:05:29) but never searched for it, and re-derived and re-wrote the identical diagnosis from scratch.

Total: **≈10.6 minutes of duplicated diagnostic work** on one root cause, in one day, across concurrent/near-concurrent sessions.

**Proposed durable fix**: This repo already has a rule for the sibling pattern (canon-push-blocked, issues #53-59: "search for the open issue by invariant identifier before re-diagnosing"). Extend that same discipline to *tool/environment* failures encountered mid-task, not just to warnings-you-can't-fix: before spending multi-minute diagnostic effort on an unexpected script/env failure during a queue-dispatched run, do one quick `search_issues` for the error's distinctive substring (e.g. "converge-item", "GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set", "could not be read") before re-deriving the cause. Separately, codify the now-confirmed-3× fact itself (`converge-item.mjs` requires a direct GitHub API token; this session type only has MCP access; see `executor.md`'s own "GitHub access is MCP-only" line) as a named, recognizable failure signature in the local pack, so a future session recognizes it immediately instead of re-tracing env vars, curl, and `gh.mjs` internals.

**Confidence**: High — durable (recurs by construction any time this queue step runs from this session type), reusable, measured, not a permission-bypass ask (the fix is "stop investigating sooner and reuse the existing diagnosis," not "route around the 403").

---

### Candidate 2 — Signal type 2 (minor)

**Evidence** (#244, ~13:01:28): agent opened PR #273 with a GitHub closing keyword in the body, then immediately caught its own mistake ("I need to fix a mistake — I added a GitHub auto-close keyword to the PR body, but this queue-managed item should stay open... the task explicitly says 'leave it for review'") and issued a follow-up `update_pull_request` call to correct it.

**Proposed fix**: Marginal — the task file already stated the correct behavior and the agent had already read it; this was a one-off attention slip, self-caught within one turn at negligible cost (one extra tool call). Not clearly durable/reusable beyond "read your own retrieved instructions before acting," which is already general practice.

**Confidence**: Low — doesn't clearly clear the durable/reusable bar; recommend not landing a rule for this alone.

---

### No new findings beyond the above
- #260's web-research dead ends (several `EGRESS_BLOCKED` fetches against cursor.com/agents.md/deepwiki.com/rulesync.dev) were each a *different* fact from a *different* domain, not repeated hits on one blocked domain — this matches, rather than violates, the existing basics/RULES.md guidance on egress blocks. No new lesson.
- #262's ~3.5 minutes re-verifying issue #192 against current `main` (executor.md retirement, tick.mjs compatibility shim) was legitimate required triage diligence (single-issue-triage's "implemented in main" verification), not waste.

# Growth-Extract Conversation Report — issue-246, issue-239, issue-243

All three logs are **queue-fired agentic sessions** (`routine-fire-payload`), not human dialogue — each begins "Read `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` and follow it." So signal types 1 (misunderstanding with a human) and 4 (recurring user questions) don't apply structurally; there is no human in the loop. All findings are type 2/3 (suboptimal agent action / wasted wall-time), and the same root cause recurs identically across all three sessions, which is itself the strongest evidence of durability.

## Finding 1 — Hand-converging an issue after `converge-item.mjs` fails violates the script's own documented remedy and clobbers labels

**Signal type:** 2 (suboptimal action, missed an already-read convention)

**Evidence:**
- `queue/instructions.md` (read by every session at step 1) says explicitly: *"Converge the issue exactly once — in code, not by hand... If the command refuses, read what it says: it means this item is not yours to converge, and doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`."*
- `engine/scheduler/signals/gh.mjs`'s own header states: *"engine/scheduler/ is the one place that legitimately uses the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` — everything session-side stays MCP-only."*
- **issue-246 log**, entries ~188–283: `converge-item.mjs` fails (403, "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). The agent then reads 4+ internal engine files (`work-item.mjs`, `run-record.mjs`, `apply-status.mjs`, `readiness.mjs`) to hand-replicate the transition, then calls `mcp__github__issue_write` with `labels: ["task:done"]` — a **full label-set overwrite** (a PUT), which the codebase's own `github.mjs` comment explicitly forbids ("LABEL WRITES ARE GRANULAR, ALWAYS... never write the label SET"). The final `issue_read` confirms labels = `["task:done"]` only — any prior queue-state labels (`task:agent`, etc.) were silently clobbered, exactly the failure mode instructions.md warned about.
- **issue-243 log**, entries ~110–265: identical pattern — same 403, ~4m56s of investigation (including searching precedent issues #242, #246, #257, #259), same wrong outcome: `issue_write` with `labels: ["task:done"]`, same clobber.
- **issue-239 log**, entries ~305–375 (contrast case): same 403 hit, but this session correctly followed instructions.md — posted a comment explaining step 6 couldn't run and left the issue for a human, with **no** `issue_write` call at all.

**Proposed durable fix:** This is a real, demonstrated inconsistency (2 of 3 sessions violated an instruction they'd just read). Since `queue/instructions.md` is canon/vendored, the fix belongs there (per this repo's own rule, as a patch-on-an-issue) — either strengthen the wording so "doing it by hand" is unambiguous even under context pressure, or add a check that flags an `issue_write` label-array call following a failed `converge-item.mjs` invocation in the same session. A cheaper local mitigation: `converge-item.mjs`'s failure message could state the remedy inline ("do not hand-replicate — comment and stop") rather than relying on the agent to recall a rule read minutes earlier.

**Confidence:** High — directly falsifies a codebase invariant, reproduced twice, with a clean contrast case showing the correct behavior was reachable.

## Finding 2 — The same ~3–5 minute `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`/403 investigation is repeated from scratch in every session

**Signal type:** 2/3 (suboptimal action + measured wasted time, recurring)

**Evidence (measured):**
- issue-246: 12:58:41 → 13:01:32 (**2m51s**) spent discovering `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` unset → setting it → hitting a 403 → reading `gh.mjs`/`converge-item.mjs` → curl-testing the token directly.
- issue-239: 13:00:53 → 13:03:41 (**2m48s**), same sequence, plus a proxy-status check.
- issue-243: 13:00:08 → 13:05:04 (**4m56s**), same sequence plus searching past issues for precedent.

All three sessions, run within the same ~15-minute window on 2026-08-23, independently rediscovered the identical root cause: `converge-item.mjs` is written for the GitHub Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (raw REST, full repo scope) and cannot succeed when invoked from an interactive/queue session, whose token returns `403 GitHub access is not enabled for this session`. This is not a fixable-from-the-session problem — no amount of curl/env investigation changes the outcome — yet each session repeated the full diagnostic (env grep, curl to the raw API, reading `gh.mjs`, proxy status) before giving up.

**Proposed durable fix:** `queue/instructions.md` step 6 should state up front that `converge-item.mjs` is Action-side only and is *expected* to fail with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` unset or a 403 when run from a session — treat either as the "refuses" case immediately, skip diagnosis, and go straight to the documented remedy (comment + leave for human, per Finding 1). This turns ~3–5 minutes of redundant, unproductive investigation per occurrence into an instant, correct branch. (Not a "route around the denial" fix — the opposite: stop trying to make the denied path work, and take the already-correct fallback faster.)

**Confidence:** Medium-high — the wall-time cost is real and measured, and the fix is a documentation change, not a workaround; but the absolute time saved per occurrence (a few minutes) is modest, which is why this is medium- rather than high-priority relative to Finding 1.

## No other durable findings

Beyond the two related findings above, nothing else in these three logs clears the bar: the `git mv`/`diff`/`cp` workflow-file collision in issue-246 was a one-off repo state, resolved in 3 quick commands; the deep git-archaeology in issue-239's growth-dedup work (reading multiple past commits, SKILL.md, prior local-pack rules) was appropriate diligence for that task, not friction; the "create then close" two-call tracker-issue pattern in issue-243 is an already-documented convention, not a new lesson.

## Log classification

- **Candidate** (yielded report-worthy signals): issue-246, issue-239, issue-243 — all three, via the shared Finding 1/2 pair above (issue-239 serves as the positive contrast case rather than a separate defect).
- **No-comment**: none of the three assigned logs.

<result># Growth-Extract Conversation Report — issue-246, issue-239, issue-243

All three logs are **queue-fired agentic sessions** (`routine-fire-payload`), not human dialogue — each begins "Read `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` and follow it." So signal types 1 (misunderstanding with a human) and 4 (recurring user questions) don't apply structurally; there is no human in the loop. All findings are type 2/3 (suboptimal agent action / wasted wall-time), and the same root cause recurs identically across all three sessions, which is itself the strongest evidence of durability.

## Finding 1 — Hand-converging an issue after `converge-item.mjs` fails violates the script's own documented remedy and clobbers labels

**Signal type:** 2 (suboptimal action, missed an already-read convention)

**Evidence:**
- `queue/instructions.md` (read by every session at step 1) says explicitly: *"Converge the issue exactly once — in code, not by hand... If the command refuses, read what it says: it means this item is not yours to converge, and doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`."*
- `engine/scheduler/signals/gh.mjs`'s own header states: *"engine/scheduler/ is the one place that legitimately uses the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` — everything session-side stays MCP-only."*
- **issue-246 log**, entries ~188–283: `converge-item.mjs` fails (403, "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). The agent then reads 4+ internal engine files (`work-item.mjs`, `run-record.mjs`, `apply-status.mjs`, `readiness.mjs`) to hand-replicate the transition, then calls `mcp__github__issue_write` with `labels: ["task:done"]` — a **full label-set overwrite** (a PUT), which the codebase's own `github.mjs` comment explicitly forbids ("LABEL WRITES ARE GRANULAR, ALWAYS... never write the label SET"). The final `issue_read` confirms labels = `["task:done"]` only — any prior queue-state labels (`task:agent`, etc.) were silently clobbered, exactly the failure mode instructions.md warned about.
- **issue-243 log**, entries ~110–265: identical pattern — same 403, ~4m56s of investigation (including searching precedent issues #242, #246, #257, #259), same wrong outcome: `issue_write` with `labels: ["task:done"]`, same clobber.
- **issue-239 log**, entries ~305–375 (contrast case): same 403 hit, but this session correctly followed instructions.md — posted a comment explaining step 6 couldn't run and left the issue for a human, with **no** `issue_write` call at all.

**Proposed durable fix:** This is a real, demonstrated inconsistency (2 of 3 sessions violated an instruction they'd just read). Since `queue/instructions.md` is canon/vendored, the fix belongs there (per this repo's own rule, as a patch-on-an-issue) — either strengthen the wording so "doing it by hand" is unambiguous even under context pressure, or add a check that flags an `issue_write` label-array call following a failed `converge-item.mjs` invocation in the same session. A cheaper local mitigation: `converge-item.mjs`'s failure message could state the remedy inline ("do not hand-replicate — comment and stop") rather than relying on the agent to recall a rule read minutes earlier.

**Confidence:** High — directly falsifies a codebase invariant, reproduced twice, with a clean contrast case showing the correct behavior was reachable.

## Finding 2 — The same ~3–5 minute `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`/403 investigation is repeated from scratch in every session

**Signal type:** 2/3 (suboptimal action + measured wasted time, recurring)

**Evidence (measured):**
- issue-246: 12:58:41 → 13:01:32 (**2m51s**) spent discovering `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` unset → setting it → hitting a 403 → reading `gh.mjs`/`converge-item.mjs` → curl-testing the token directly.
- issue-239: 13:00:53 → 13:03:41 (**2m48s**), same sequence, plus a proxy-status check.
- issue-243: 13:00:08 → 13:05:04 (**4m56s**), same sequence plus searching past issues for precedent.

All three sessions, run within the same ~15-minute window on 2026-08-23, independently rediscovered the identical root cause: `converge-item.mjs` is written for the GitHub Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (raw REST, full repo scope) and cannot succeed when invoked from an interactive/queue session, whose token returns `403 GitHub access is not enabled for this session`. This is not a fixable-from-the-session problem — no amount of curl/env investigation changes the outcome — yet each session repeated the full diagnostic (env grep, curl to the raw API, reading `gh.mjs`, proxy status) before giving up.

**Proposed durable fix:** `queue/instructions.md` step 6 should state up front that `converge-item.mjs` is Action-side only and is *expected* to fail with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` unset or a 403 when run from a session — treat either as the "refuses" case immediately, skip diagnosis, and go straight to the documented remedy (comment + leave for human, per Finding 1). This turns ~3–5 minutes of redundant, unproductive investigation per occurrence into an instant, correct branch. (Not a "route around the denial" fix — the opposite: stop trying to make the denied path work, and take the already-correct fallback faster.)

**Confidence:** Medium-high — the wall-time cost is real and measured, and the fix is a documentation change, not a workaround; but the absolute time saved per occurrence (a few minutes) is modest, which is why this is medium- rather than high-priority relative to Finding 1.

## No other durable findings

Beyond the two related findings above, nothing else in these three logs clears the bar: the `git mv`/`diff`/`cp` workflow-file collision in issue-246 was a one-off repo state, resolved in 3 quick commands; the deep git-archaeology in issue-239's growth-dedup work (reading multiple past commits, SKILL.md, prior local-pack rules) was appropriate diligence for that task, not friction; the "create then close" two-call tracker-issue pattern in issue-243 is an already-documented convention, not a new lesson.

## Log classification

- **Candidate** (yielded report-worthy signals): issue-246, issue-239, issue-243 — all three, via the shared Finding 1/2 pair above (issue-239 serves as the positive contrast case rather than a separate defect).
- **No-comment**: none of the three assigned logs.</result>

## Report: Conversation-log lessons (issue-253, issue-261, issue-240)

### Log: issue-253 (site reframe — human-directed session, ~15 min)

**Candidate 1 — Signal type 2 (suboptimal action / missed convention)**
Evidence: entries ~113–123. `SendUserFile` rejected `site-mobile.jpg` (full downscaled mobile shot) and then rejected two half-height splits (~9,100px tall, ~0.5MiB each) with `server returned 400`. Only quartering (~4,266px tall) succeeded. The agent reasoned "likely a dimension cap, not just bytes" only after two failed round-trips.
Proposed fix: the project's `site-visual-check` skill already documents a byte/width rule ("downscale to 600–720px wide") but says nothing about image **height**. Add a line noting mobile full-page shots must also be pre-split by height (quarters, not halves) before delivery, since the delivery channel enforces a max pixel height independent of width/bytes.
Confidence: high — concrete, reusable, and the skill file is the obvious, already-identified home for it.

**Candidate 2 — Signal type 2 (redundant diagnosis, possibly duplicated known issue)**
Evidence: entries ~137–190. CI failed twice (`pull_request` runs) with jobs completing in ~2s, `runner_id:0`, no runner assigned — the agent spent ~5 minutes (12:37:58→12:42:32) forensically diagnosing this via job/run metadata and comparing to neighboring runs before merging past the still-red check. Separately, log-240's `list_issues` (12:55) shows issue **#256**, "GitHub Actions can't provision runners in this repo since 2026-08-21 — check the Actions spending limit," already closed — the same failure signature (runner provisioning), for the same repo, same window.
Proposed fix: before spending minutes reconstructing a CI-infra diagnosis from raw job metadata, search open/closed issues for an existing incident report first (keywords: "runner", "provision", "spending limit"). If one exists and is closed/known, cite it and proceed; don't re-derive from scratch each time.
Confidence: medium — the exact timing of #256 relative to log-253's investigation isn't fully confirmed from these logs, but the pattern (recognizable failure signature, no issue search performed) is real and the fix is cheap and durable.

### Logs: issue-261 and issue-240 (concurrent queue-fired tidy/growth tasks, same ~10-min window)

**Candidate 3 — Signal type 2 + 4 (recurring redundant diagnosis across sessions), MEASURED**
Both are unattended, queue-fired sessions run almost simultaneously (stamps `1300Z` and `1301Z`). Both independently hit the same wall at the mandated terminal-transition step (`converge-item.mjs`, called per `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` step 6):

- issue-261: `converge-item.mjs` fails first with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY is not set`, then `#261 could not be read` after that's set; the session tries alternate tokens, checks the proxy status/README, greps hooks — 12:57:17 → 13:00:25 ≈ **3m08s** — then falls back to a plain MCP comment only (no defect issue filed, no confirmation the item was actually parked correctly per the protocol's `needs-human-action` label).
- issue-240: hits the identical failure, diagnoses more thoroughly (direct `gh.mjs` probe → `401 Bad credentials` → proxy trace → `403 GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App`) — 12:56:02 → 13:01:14 ≈ **5m12s** — then correctly files a "Canon defect: converge-item.mjs cannot run session-side" issue (#274) and leaves #240 with an explanatory comment only, no label/close.

Combined: **~8m20s of duplicated diagnosis of one root cause**, produced independently by two sessions running at the same time, with only one of the two leaving a durable trace (#274) that the other could have used had it searched first, and had #274 existed yet.

Proposed fix (durable, reusable — this is exactly the shape the project's own `basics` pack already names: "handing over a step only a human can perform" → its own issue): 
1. Before re-diagnosing a `converge-item.mjs` failure, search issues for an existing "Canon defect: converge-item.mjs..." report — the diagnosis (session-side sessions lack direct GitHub REST; only MCP works) is now known and shouldn't be re-derived.
2. When `converge-item.mjs` cannot run for this reason, the correct, minimal path is: plain comment on the item explaining state + pointer to the canon-defect issue, no label/close touched (per the instructions file's own "doing it by hand is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`" warning) — issue-240's handling is the template; issue-261's is a partial miss (no defect issue referenced/filed, leaving no trace for the next session).
3. Since the underlying cause is "an org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App" for this session type, and this is a standing environment gap (not a one-off flake), that same defect issue is the right home for a human hand-off — it should stay open until an admin acts, rather than being silently rediscovered every time a queue-fired session runs.

Confidence: high — this is a measured, recurring, concrete cost with a clear low-effort fix (search-before-diagnose, plus templating on #240's already-correct handling), squarely fitting the "durable, reusable, generalizable" bar and not a permission-bypass rule (the fix is "stop and hand off correctly," never "retry past the block").

### No-comment items
Nothing else in these three logs cleared the bar: tool batching/parallelism looked already sound (Reads/Globs issued together), the `node --test` misinvocation in log-253 self-corrected in one turn, and the background-timer CI polling in log-253 was appropriately sized (not blind/padded sleeps) — none of these are worth a new rule.

### Summary
- **Candidate logs**: 2026-08-23T1242Z--issue-253 (2 findings), 2026-08-23T1300Z--issue-261 + 2026-08-23T1301Z--issue-240 (1 shared, measured finding spanning both).
- **No-comment logs**: none — all three contributed at least one report-worthy signal, though issue-253's second finding is medium confidence and the strongest, highest-confidence signal is the converge-item.mjs cross-session duplication (candidate 3).

1	---
2	name: site-visual-check
3	description: Screenshot and visually verify site/ (claudinite.com), desktop and mobile, and deliver the result to the owner. Use when changing site/ markup, CSS, or animations, or when checking responsive/mobile rendering.
4	---
5	
6	The site is static and dependency-free, so verification is: serve `site/`, render it
7	in a real browser, look at the image. Do that on **every** change to `site/` — the
8	page is iterated frequently and unreviewed.
9	
10	## Serve it
11	
12	```
13	(python3 -m http.server 8321 -d site >/dev/null 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
14	```
15	
16	Kill the server once the last shot is taken; don't leave it running for the rest
17	of the session.
18	
19	## Desktop shots
20	
21	`chrome --headless --screenshot` is fine **for desktop widths**:
22	
23	```
24	/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome --headless --disable-gpu \
25	  --no-sandbox --window-size=1440,8400 --virtual-time-budget=8000 \
26	  --hide-scrollbars --screenshot=$SP/full.png "http://localhost:8321/"
27	```
28	
29	`--virtual-time-budget` must outlast the reveal-on-scroll and mechanism
30	animations, or sections render mid-transition and look broken when they aren't.
31	A full-page PNG is too tall to read in one go — crop it into sections with
32	Pillow before viewing.
33	
34	## Mobile — do NOT use `--window-size` to fake a phone viewport

---
name: site-visual-check
description: Screenshot and visually verify site/ (claudinite.com), desktop and mobile, and deliver the result to the owner. Use when changing site/ markup, CSS, or animations, or when checking responsive/mobile rendering.
---

The site is static and dependency-free, so verification is: serve `site/`, render it
in a real browser, look at the image. Do that on **every** change to `site/` — the
page is iterated frequently and unreviewed.

## Serve it

```
(python3 -m http.server 8321 -d site >/dev/null 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
```

Kill the server once the last shot is taken; don't leave it running for the rest
of the session.

## Desktop shots

`chrome --headless --screenshot` is fine **for desktop widths**:

```
/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome --headless --disable-gpu \
  --no-sandbox --window-size=1440,8400 --virtual-time-budget=8000 \
  --hide-scrollbars --screenshot=$SP/full.png "http://localhost:8321/"
```

`--virtual-time-budget` must outlast the reveal-on-scroll and mechanism
animations, or sections render mid-transition and look broken when they aren't.
A full-page PNG is too tall to read in one go — crop it into sections with
Pillow before viewing.

## Mobile — do NOT use `--window-size` to fake a phone viewport

**Footgun, and it costs a whole phantom bug hunt.** A narrow
`--window-size=390,9500` headless shot renders the page at a *clamped* width and
crops content at the right edge. That looks exactly like a horizontal-overflow
bug across every section, and it is not one — the layout is fine at a real 390px
viewport. Don't start instrumenting CSS to find the "offender."

For any width below desktop, drive a real browser context instead:

```js
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';  // npm i playwright-core in scratch
const b = await chromium.launch({
  executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome',
  args: ['--no-sandbox'],
});
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
                            deviceScaleFactor: 2 });
await p.goto('http://localhost:8321/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
await p.screenshot({ path: 'mobile.png', fullPage: true });
await b.close();
```

`newContext`/`newPage` with an explicit `viewport` is what actually applies the
media queries; the CLI flag does not.

## Show the owner

A raw full-page capture is rejected as too large — downscale to roughly 600–720px
wide and send it as JPEG (quality ~82), alongside a full-size hero crop.

33	asserting which entities exist, what a surface must render, or that a feature's parts are wired to
34	each other is a **requirement**; its home is the project's executable spec and the suite that proves

42	quality — a product statement converts into a genuinely well-made check, clean parse and see-it-fail proof and
43	all, and is still the wrong kind. The discriminator, applied **before** you write anything: *if the product
44	changed its mind tomorrow, would this rule be wrong?* Wrong → it's a requirement, and a red check would report
45	a product decision as a process violation. Still true whatever the product decides → it's a working rule.
46

48	re-home it. **Leave the prose and log it** as a mis-homed rule, the same way an un-checkable
49	candidate is logged — never cement it as a check.

53	For each rule that cleared the gate, ask the one question from
54	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
55	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**

57	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
58	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
59	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
60	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
61	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
62	
63	**"Already covered by another check" is a claim to test, not to reason out** — hand the sibling check a file
64	that violates the rule before dropping the candidate as a duplicate. A ban list only covers the routes whoever
65	wrote it thought of, so the routes it misses are invisible to exactly the reasoning that drew it: three sweeps
66	running dropped an "the app opens no socket" rule because a neighbouring check banned the obvious networking
67	import, while the base library re-exported a raw socket call that sailed straight through.
68

70	re-derive it against today's sources.** A removal, a migration or a consolidation can collapse the entry points
71	a rule had to cover, and the objection dies with them: a "one deletable storage directory" rule needed
72	data-flow tracing while many entry points wrote paths, and needed none once one root remained. So when a sweep
73	meets prose an earlier sweep left behind, re-ask the question rather than trusting the recorded answer. (This
74	covers the *technical* verdict only — an owner's rejection of a conversion is settled.)
75	
76	**Read the conversion tracker's prior comments before authoring, not after.** Independent re-derivation is
77	exactly how duplicate work happens: a fresh reading of the same prose will happily re-nominate a rule, build it
78	out in full, and only then discover it was built and rejected before. The tracker is a precondition of the
79	work, not a place to log it — and record each rejection with its reason so the next run can act on it.
80	
81	**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
82	— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
83	answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
84	where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.
85	
86	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
87	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
88

90	
91	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
92	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
93	
94	> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
95	> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
96	> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.
97	
98	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack, at the ladder's highest check rung the rule allows: an entry
99	   in `<pack>/declared-checks.json` when its logic is patterns over files, dropping to `<pack>/<rule>.mjs`
100	   listed in `pack.mjs` only when it needs what patterns can't say. Either way the failure message *is*
101	   the rule (what / why / fix — plus, for a rule module, the `doc:` pointer back to the prose; a
102	   declaration carries no pointer and must state its own case).
103	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
104	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
105	   doesn't ship.
106	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory when the rule is
107	   directional by kind, or when the condition is blocking-grade but **irreversible by the time it is
108	   observable** (an append-only transcript, a published artifact). A blocking finding no edit can
109	   retract never converges — it spends every remaining Stop cycle on something nothing can fix.
110	   Advisory there is *diagnostic*: it names the cause the moment it appears.
111	   - **Prefer a positive allowlist over an enumerated list of the bad cases.** Match the one allowed
112	     shape and flag everything else, rather than banning the violations you can name. An allowlist
113	     catches a variant that doesn't exist yet the day it lands, and turns an indirection (a value
114	     passed through a variable instead of written literally) into a finding too — refusing to reason
115	     about indirection is the feature. Invert only where the allowed set is genuinely open-ended.
116	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
117	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
118	
119	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
120	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
121	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
122	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
123	check to the same fixture bar.
124	
125	**When a rule mandates a *form*, the check asserts that form — never the intent behind it.** Where
126	the prose says *write it exactly like this*, the check's whole job is deciding whether the artifact
127	is that form; inferring what the author meant is unbounded in the wrong direction and leaves the
128	likeliest reproduction uncaught, since a hand-picked marker list always misses the phrasing nobody
129	enumerated. Expect a form check to fire on something that breaks the form while causing no harm —
130	that's the rule as written doing its job, not a reason to re-add intent-guessing.

133	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.

139	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent

16	  behaviour.

19	  here — preserve it as a patch on an issue in this repo rather than routing
20	  around the block.** Work in this repo lands in canon code often (#53, #54, #55
21	  and #57 were all defects in the vendored engine and packs, found from here), and
22	  a scratch clone of the canon is read-only in practice: the git proxy
23	  serves `missingbulb/Claudinite` for a fetch but `403`s a push, because a
24	  session's GitHub scope is `missingbulb/claudinitewebsite` alone. That is an

  remote or a token, and don't edit the vendored `.claudinite/shared/` mount in
  place to compensate — baselining re-vendors it and the edit vanishes. Finish
  and test the change in the scratch canon clone, then open an issue here
  carrying the full `git diff` as a patch block plus the verification you ran
  (#59 is the shape), so a session that does have canon scope can `git apply` it.

- **A file missing from the mount is evidence about the *vendor set*, not about
  the canon — read the canon before an issue names the gap.** Three
  queue-dispatched sessions on 2026-08-16/17 found
  `engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md` absent from `.claudinite/shared/`,
  and two filed it (#190, #192) as the canon never having shipped it, both
  saying they had "no way to tell which from here." A third shallow-cloned
  `missingbulb/Claudinite` and found the file present — a vendoring omission, so
  #192's ask to author it would have produced a duplicate of a file that already
  existed. The scratch canon clone the rule above names is read-only, but it
  *reads*: use it, and where it still can't settle the cause, report only that
  the mount lacks the file.

- **After a merge lands on GitHub, syncing local `main` is a convenience, not part
  of landing — if the environment refuses it, record that and stop, don't retry
  variants.** `git checkout main` and its neighbours are refused by the session's
  permission classifier here; the two merge sessions on 2026-08-01 hit five straight
  denials between them, one of them after three rephrasings of the same intent
  (`checkout && pull`, then bare `checkout`, then `fetch origin main`), burning about
  four minutes on a step with nothing downstream of it. The `merge-to-main` recipe's
  sync step exists so *your working copy* isn't stale; the squash-merge already
  happened server-side and `merge_pull_request` returning `"merged":true` is the
  whole proof. Take one attempt, and on a refusal say plainly that local `main` is
  behind and move to the next step (the growth-pack capture) rather than looking for
  a phrasing that gets through.

- **`mcp__github__search_issues`/`list_issues` located by title (`in:title`) can
  blow the MCP token limit — this repo's tracker issues (`Claudinite tracker:
  <dimension>`) accumulate long comment histories, so a bare title search returns
  every match's full body and errors before it returns anything.** Pass
  `fields: ["number", "title", "state"]` (or similarly narrow) on the *first* call
  whenever the search is only locating an issue by title, not after the "exceeds
  maximum allowed tokens" error forces a retry. Hit independently in three separate
  scheduled runs (issues #159, #161, #168), each paying a wasted round-trip (and,
  twice, a manual dump-and-reparse) for a result the narrowed call answers cleanly.

- **Never amend a subagent's already-pushed commit, and never relay a fabricated
  "fix" instruction for a check that doesn't exist as described, when a
  mid-dispatch Stop-hook finding turns out to be a background subagent's shared
  checkout misread as your own.** Issue #98: the orchestrator sent the subagent
  exactly such an instruction (which the subagent correctly refused as looking
  like an injection) and attempted `git commit --amend` on the subagent's
  already-pushed commit — blocked only by the permission classifier. **If the
  checkout-back or the amend is itself refused by the permission classifier,
  don't retry or force it** — a live subagent is using the shared checkout. Issue
  #116 hit exactly this: both remedies were blocked mid-run, and the orchestrator
  correctly left the branch untouched and waited; the branch reverted to the
  orchestrator's own assigned one, and the false-positive noise with it, the
  moment the subagent finished.

- **After a background subagent's handle goes unreachable following a genuine
  worker-restart notice, checking only git log/status and the dispatch PR's own
  comments is not enough to tell whether it made progress — it may already have
  filed a GitHub issue.** In issue #112, a subagent found a blocking finding and
  filed issue #113 moments before its worker restarted. The orchestrator's recovery
  check covered only git and PR-comment state (both clean, since the subagent's
  real output was a filed issue, not a commit), concluded "no progress survived,"
  and relaunched a second subagent from a from-scratch briefing — which
  re-investigated the same root cause and filed a duplicate, issue #114, wasting
  about 5m42s of redundant subagent work. Before asserting "no progress" in a
  relaunch briefing after a worker-restart, also search GitHub issues
  (`search_issues`/`list_issues`) for anything the lost subagent may have filed —
  not just the dispatch PR's own comments and local git log.

---
name: site-visual-check
description: Screenshot and visually verify site/ (claudinite.com), desktop and mobile, and deliver the result to the owner. Use when changing site/ markup, CSS, or animations, or when checking responsive/mobile rendering.
---

The site is static and dependency-free, so verification is: serve `site/`, render it
in a real browser, look at the image. Do that on **every** change to `site/` — the
page is iterated frequently and unreviewed.

## Serve it

```
(python3 -m http.server 8321 -d site >/dev/null 2>&1 &) && sleep 1
```

Kill the server once the last shot is taken; don't leave it running for the rest
of the session.

## Desktop shots

`chrome --headless --screenshot` is fine **for desktop widths**:

```
/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome --headless --disable-gpu \
  --no-sandbox --window-size=1440,8400 --virtual-time-budget=8000 \
  --hide-scrollbars --screenshot=$SP/full.png "http://localhost:8321/"
```

`--virtual-time-budget` must outlast the reveal-on-scroll and mechanism
animations, or sections render mid-transition and look broken when they aren't.
A full-page PNG is too tall to read in one go — crop it into sections with
Pillow before viewing.

## Mobile — do NOT use `--window-size` to fake a phone viewport

**Footgun, and it costs a whole phantom bug hunt.** A narrow
`--window-size=390,9500` headless shot renders the page at a *clamped* width and
crops content at the right edge. That looks exactly like a horizontal-overflow
bug across every section, and it is not one — the layout is fine at a real 390px
viewport. Don't start instrumenting CSS to find the "offender."

For any width below desktop, drive a real browser context instead:

```js
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';  // npm i playwright-core in scratch
const b = await chromium.launch({
  executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome',
  args: ['--no-sandbox'],
});
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
                            deviceScaleFactor: 2 });
await p.goto('http://localhost:8321/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
await p.screenshot({ path: 'mobile.png', fullPage: true });
await b.close();
```

`newContext`/`newPage` with an explicit `viewport` is what actually applies the
media queries; the CLI flag does not.

A raw full-page capture is rejected as too large — downscale to roughly 600–720px
wide and send it as JPEG (quality ~82), alongside a full-size hero crop.

Growth-extract pass over the window named in #241's Context (commits f7dd143, df00e1e; merged PRs #269, #254; touched PRs #273, #263; touched issues #277, #204, #54, #255, #274, #264; conversation logs on `conversation-logs` — hindsight window from `2026-08-13T2146Z`, fresh window `2026-08-23T*`).

## Activity half — no new lessons

Both signal-bearing findings in the window's commits/PRs/issues are out of scope for a local-pack rule:
- The `converge-item.mjs` session-side failure (#274, #277) is an engine defect, already filed upstream — not something a project rule fixes.
- The egress-block and site-self-description signals (PR #263, issue #255) are already covered by existing rules (`html`/`basics` packs' egress-block guidance; this pack's own "site describes itself" rule, which #263 is itself an instance of working correctly).

## Conversation half — two lessons landed

1. **`RULES.md`** — a `queue/instructions.md` step 6 `converge-item.mjs` failure is a known, standing gap for this session type (MCP-only credential vs. the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`). Seven work-item sessions in one day independently spent 2–5 minutes each re-deriving the same root cause; two made it worse by hand-replicating the labeling transition via `mcp__github__issue_write`'s `labels` field, which is a full-set overwrite that silently clobbered queue-state labels. Captured so a future session recognizes the failure immediately and follows `instructions.md`'s own remedy (comment + leave for a human) instead.
2. **`skills/site-visual-check/SKILL.md`** — a tall mobile screenshot can still be rejected (`400`) by pixel height after the existing width/byte downscale; split into height quarters, not halves, before sending.

Both are runtime/judgment knowledge (no static repo artifact to scan), so both stay as prose per the promotion ladder — no check conversion applies.

## Verification

- `node --test .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite-website/*.test.mjs` — 27/27 pass
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — clean (exit 0)

`VERSIONS.md` (previously missing for this pack) created with both rows.

Refs #241
